caption: 01 · CODE — Can the eye be explained?. A code is not a mood board. It is a set of recurring decisions—silhouette, proportion, material, finish, behavior, refusal—with examples, exceptions, and a reason for each. The test is not whether every object looks alike. It is whether a collaborator can recognize the governing judgment.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can the eye be explained? within When Does a Designer Become a House?.

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · CARRY — Can another hand act without impersonating?. An institution needs roles, handoffs, review rituals, and vocabulary. Documentation should transmit the standard while leaving room for skilled interpretation. If every decision must return to the founder, the practice has staff but not institutional capacity.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can another hand act without impersonating? within When Does a Designer Become a House?.

caption: 03 · PROOF — Can the work prove its own making?. Collection records, samples, specifications, correspondence, credits, rights decisions, and accession-quality metadata turn memory into evidence. The record does not replace the object; it prevents the object from becoming anonymous.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can the work prove its own making? within When Does a Designer Become a House?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · CONTINUITY — Can the system survive absence?. A house is tested by illness, departure, conflict, growth, sale, and succession. Continuity requires named authority, access to accounts and files, an archive, and a method for distinguishing evolution from imitation.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
